The reaction was initially at pH 1, meaning a high concentration of H⁺ ions. The product contains H⁺, so H⁺ is likely a reactant or catalyst. When the unknown substance fell in, it caused an exothermic reaction that raised the pH to 4 (decreased H⁺ concentration). A lower H⁺ concentration would slow the reaction rate. Although the temperature increased (which would typically speed up the reaction), the observed rate slowed, indicating the pH increase was the dominant factor. Increased pressure or volume are not relevant to the described changes.

Answer: A
